trial_court: District Judge of Midnapore, Suit No. 27 of 1957
case_name: Ajit Kumar Bhunia vs Sm. Kanan Bala Deyi
facts_of_case: Petitioner, as husband, instituted suit for dissolution of marriage with respondent under Section 13 of Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. The suit was transferred to Additional District Judge, Midnapore, and the petitioner then filed an application challenging the jurisdiction of the learned Additional District Judge.

legal_principles.principle: The Additional District Judge has, on transfer or assignment of a particular case to him by the learned District Judge under Section 8 of the Bengal, Agra and Assam Civil Courts Act, all the powers, authority and jurisdiction of the learned District Judge himself, so far as that case is concerned.
applicable_acts_sections: Bengal, Agra and Assam Civil Courts Act — Section 8
cited_cases: Rup Keshwar Lal v. Mt. Jaijai Bibi, (1916) Cal WN 791
Mohator Rahman v. Abdur Rahim, ILR 48 Cal 53

legal_principles.principle: The Supreme Court's decision has not overruled the practically unanimous view of this Court on the question of jurisdiction of the learned Additional District Judges and on the effect of transfer (assignment) of cases to them by the learned District Judge.
cited_cases: Mutsaddi Lal v. Mule Mal, ILR 34 All 205
Makhan Lal v. Ajit Kumar Bhunia, (1960) Cal WN 382

outcome.final_order: The question of jurisdiction of the learned Additional District Judges is decided in favour of the petitioner.

keywords: Bengal Agra and Assam Civil Courts Act
Kuldip Singh v. The State of Punjab
